features.name: checking_status_ordinal
features.description: Ordinal encoding of checking account status from most negative to most positive balance, with no checking account as a separate high-risk indicator mapped to 0
features.expected_model_benefit: Enables tree splits on ordered checking account balance levels, capturing monotonic risk relationship

features.name: savings_status_ordinal
features.description: Ordinal encoding of savings account status from lowest to highest balance tier
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides ordered savings level for tree splits, capturing wealth buffer effect on creditworthiness
features.formula: np.where(savings_status == 'no known savings', 0, np.where(savings_status == '<100', 1, np.where(savings_status == '100<=X<500', 2, np.where(savings_status == '500<=X<1000', 3, np.where(savings_status == '>=1000', 4, 0)))))

features.name: employment_ordinal
features.description: Ordinal encoding of employment duration from unemployed to longest tenure
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures employment stability as ordered feature for tree splits on job security

features.name: monthly_payment_burden
features.description: Estimated monthly payment as credit amount divided by duration, scaled by installment commitment rate
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures monthly financial burden combining loan size, duration, and commitment rate for tree splits

features.name: log_credit_amount
features.description: Log-transformed credit amount to compress right-skewed distribution for better tree splits
features.expected_model_benefit: Reduces skewness in credit amount, enabling more balanced tree splits across loan size range

features.name: high_risk_checking_flag
features.description: Binary flag indicating negative or no checking account balance, both associated with higher financial risk
features.expected_model_benefit: Direct boolean split on most predictive checking account risk categories

features.name: credit_history_risk_score
features.description: Numeric risk score derived from credit history category, with higher values indicating worse credit history
features.expected_model_benefit: Converts nominal credit history into ordered risk scale for effective tree splits
features.formula: np.where(credit_history == 'all paid', 4, np.where(credit_history == 'no credits/all paid', 3, np.where(credit_history == 'delayed previously', 2, np.where(credit_history == 'existing paid', 1, np.where(credit_history == 'critical/other existing credit', 0, 2)))))

features.name: long_duration_high_amount_flag
features.description: Binary flag for loans that are both long duration (above 24 months) and high amount (above mean credit amount of 3778)
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures interaction between loan size and duration as a combined risk indicator for tree splits

features.name: property_security_score
features.description: Ordinal score for property collateral quality from no property to real estate
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides ordered collateral quality measure enabling tree splits on asset security
features.formula: np.where(property_magnitude == 'no known property', 0, np.where(property_magnitude == 'life insurance', 1, np.where(property_magnitude == 'car', 2, np.where(property_magnitude == 'real estate', 3, 0))))

features.name: age_employment_stability_score
features.description: Combined score of age bucket and employment duration ordinal, capturing life-stage financial stability
features.expected_model_benefit: Nonlinear interaction between age and employment tenure captures career stability patterns for tree splits
features.formula: np.where(age < 25, 0, np.where(age < 35, 1, np.where(age < 50, 2, 3))) + np.where(employment == 'unemployed', 0, np.where(employment == '<1', 1, np.where(employment == '1<=X<4', 2, np.where(employment == '4<=X<7', 3, np.where(employment == '>=7', 5, 0)))))

features.name: financial_vulnerability_index
features.description: Semantic assessment of overall financial vulnerability combining checking account status, savings level, and employment stability into a composite risk score. Score 0 indicates strong financial position (positive checking, high savings, stable employment), score 10 indicates maximum vulnerability (negative checking, no savings, unemployed).
features.expected_model_benefit: Holistic financial vulnerability measure captures multi-dimensional risk that individual features may miss, providing strong tree split candidates

features.name: loan_purpose_risk_tier
features.description: Semantic risk tier for loan purpose based on typical repayment patterns and asset backing. Tier 1 (lowest risk, value 1): used car, real estate-backed purposes. Tier 2 (moderate risk, value 2): radio/tv, furniture/equipment, domestic appliance. Tier 3 (higher risk, value 3): new car, business, education. Tier 4 (highest risk, value 4): repairs, retraining, other unspecified purposes.
features.expected_model_benefit: Groups loan purposes by semantic risk profile enabling tree splits on purpose-based risk tiers rather than individual categories
